scope: ONE bounded new diagnostic-source and directly relevant motion-retention boundary inspection, while the immutable replay runs. No broad closed-source review or new test/native campaign.

instrumentation_assessment.answer_and_predicate: model_host.rs564-578 calls the dump only after observe has computed the Recorded difference, and returns the original observation unchanged. No mirror mask, candidate answer or physical predicate is replaced.
instrumentation_assessment.step_order: movement.rs1900-1917 retains dispatch order and its original outcome/error propagation. It inserts a trace note after dispatch and before the existing previous_position/rotor result handling. Accepted/refused status is logged, not used to decide. No callback, solver step or getter is added.
instrumentation_assessment.bind_and_retire: After existing bind validation, note_bind records raw initial state before the same physical record insertion. Retire removes the diagnostic history; it does not decide registry lifetime. These are diagnostic maps, not a second pose authority.
instrumentation_assessment.RNG: No campaign/CRT/entity RNG call or reseed is added. Extra standard-library allocation/hash bookkeeping and wall-time overhead exist; no physical decision reads them.
instrumentation_assessment.FPU: The added value capture uses to_bits, integer counters/maps, and integer/hex formatting. The formula diagnostic calls the existing integer product_toward_zero. No new physical floating-point operation/comparison is introduced. File/format library internals were not measured as a new caller-FPU proof; existing engine fatal/restore behavior is unchanged.
instrumentation_assessment.bounds: The ring is bounded to16 entries per currently traced identity; operation names are static Request names and counters are integer. The number of identity histories follows bind/retire activity rather than a new fixed global16-entry cap.
observational_limits: Every request is represented only after dispatch, so a refused request can show the record state after whatever the original dispatch did; accepted=false is not an atomic rollback claim.
No request arguments, returned Outcome.motion_vector, Core application event or simulated frame/time stamp is retained in the ring.
Only the last16 requests remain; lifetime per-name counts and the bind snapshot survive until retire, but neither proves a complete event sequence.
Retirement removes history and issued-without-record identities have no bind trace; absence of history is not universal lifetime coverage.
Dump creation/write/flush errors are ignored and dumping is enabled only by EECH_POSE_MOTION_DIAG. An absent file alone is not proof that no mismatch occurred. No current replay process was modified.
The new file is append-based. In this native path the same mirror failure normally stops the engine immediately after the reply; the instrumentation itself is not a universal first-record-only latch.

single_source_supported_candidate.category: Completed active hosted Person movement returns a vector without retaining it in the canonical record

locations.fact: PersonBegin dispatches begin_person(record,...) directly; PersonEnd does the same for end_person at2267.
begin_person either stages a pending terrain-follow step or calls settle_person(&mut record.pose,...).
end_person consumes the pending step and calls settle_person(&mut record.pose,...).
settle_person calls the real eech_person_settle solver, computes Outcome.motion_vector and returns it, but receives only &mut Pose and cannot update Record.motion_vector.
dispatch returns result without a common motion-vector retention epilogue; step only updates previous_position and rotor after dispatch.
The compiled apply_person_pose applies attitude and position, then speed and result.motion_vector[0..2] to the real Core person.
PersonBegin calls apply_person_pose only when !result.pending. PersonEnd at1799 calls it for the completed end.
The active EECH_CAMPAIGN_HOST_MOVEMENT branch calls these person begin/end adapters. Its raw legacy vector expressions below368 are #else and are not the relevant writer.
The vehicle mobile-collision flag is true and inherited by Person, so a live hosted person can be offered to collision.

single_source_supported_candidate.why_relevant: A completed host-computed infantry step can leave the canonical motion vector at its bind/previous value while C applies the newly returned vector. A later ENTITY_POSE can therefore report an actual bit4 mismatch; bit16 may additionally reflect formula diagnostics. This is a concrete source inconsistency independently of which actor the current failed replay eventually identifies.
single_source_supported_candidate.not_an_actual_actor_diagnosis: No actor/type/history trace is available to this reviewer yet. It is not established that the four failed ordinary runs reached this particular Person boundary or that it is their only defect.
single_source_supported_candidate.minimum_legitimate_fix_boundary: Retain the exact vector already computed by the Host solver at each completed person step: non-pending PersonBegin and completed PersonEnd. Do not publish the pending begin placeholder vector as physical state, read/copy Core words at query time, add a fallback, suppress mismatch4 or alter the original solver/order.
single_source_supported_candidate.earlier_prose_superseded: Any earlier assertion that persons only retain their bind seed because the legacy ps_move vector writer is excluded is incomplete: apply_person_pose is the actual active hosted writer. The old kind-1-only observer supplied no Person coverage.

can_show: Whether the actual mismatching record has Kind::Person and the observed entity type/alive/stage
Its raw Core-vs-held difference and bind vector, current pose/vector/state flags
Recent accepted PersonBegin/PersonEnd names plus post-dispatch held-vector/position/scalar words and global request sequence
Whether no canonical motion update appears in the bounded recent history despite a changed Core motion at observation
cannot_alone_show: The returned motion words of a PersonBegin/End: the ring logs retained record words only
Whether Core immediately applied that exact returned result or another raw writer changed it after application
The exact C application point or first frame/time of a divergence; a sequence counter is not a frame clock
A complete old lifecycle if the responsible request fell outside the last16 entries
trace_discrimination.smallest_conditional_additional_fact: If the mismatch actor/history is Person and the present trace cannot discriminate a later Core write, record the successful request Outcome.motion_vector plus pending status as raw words alongside the existing held-after entry. That distinguishes returned physical result from retained state without another store/solver or generic tracing framework. A bounded C apply marker is needed only if that still leaves an actual later-write ambiguity. Do not restart the active replay for this possibility.

other_directly_relevant_boundaries_check: Routed missing-waypoint and stopped/engaging branches call the Host RoutedVector helper at rv_move264/302; their legacy formulas inside#else do not establish active bypasses. Stop deliberately retains old motion until the real recomputation boundary, as Core does. No actor-specific defect was inferred there.

Ground fall uses separate candidate/gravity/settle/vector/commit phases. The Host stages settle output and C applies gravity/vector at their declared points; formula16 alone is not evidence of a held-motion mismatch. No new complete late-lifecycle clearance is claimed.

A timing window exists between Host Advance retaining its result vector (movement.rs2222) and C copying result.motion_vector after the position setter (rv_hostmv.c398-405). The position setter sends dependent/special-effect notifications (vh_vec3d.c165-232). No query-reentry in that interval was established, so this is only a conditional boundary to inspect if the actual actor/history points there, not another finding or permission to reorder Core writes.

actual_replay_status.scope: No replay outcome/first failing actor or corrected-production clearance is established by this source note. Root owns the running process and eventual actual trace join.

publication_safety: No actor IDs, raw trajectory/pose/motion words, coordinates or retail tables are included. The private source-supported candidate is described by type and source locations only.
